harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a route-based, PSK-authenticated IKEv2 IPsec site-to-site tunnel between node1 and node2 (both OPNsense 26.1.2) over their transit link, carrying node3's private LAN (10.10.10.0/24, lan-a) and node4's private LAN (10.20.20.0/24, lan-b) so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address with traffic encrypted end-to-end. Verified with tcpdump that only ESP packets cross the transit link (no plaintext). Restarted all 4 nodes one at a time (quorum preserved) and confirmed boot-identity change plus full automatic recovery of interfaces, IKE/child SAs, and firewall rules, and re-verified bidirectional connectivity node3<->node4 after all restarts.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via ARP: node1 vtnet1<->node2 vtnet1 (transit), node1 vtnet2<->node3 enp8s0 (lan-a), node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0 (lan-b); vtnet0/enp1s0 on all nodes is a separate shared management network unrelated to the task topology.
Assigned static addressing: transit 10.99.99.1/10.99.99.2 (/30); lan-a 10.10.10.0/24 (node1=.1, node3=.2); lan-b 10.20.20.0/24 (node2=.1, node4=.2).
Generated a PSK on node1 with openssl and passed it to both nodes only via secret_env, never in command text or this report.

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 and node2 via Python/ElementTree to add opt1/opt2 interfaces, firewall pass rules (lan-a/lan-b egress, IKE/ESP from the transit peer), OPNsense/IPsec preSharedKeys, and OPNsense/Swanctl Connections/locals/remotes/children (IKEv2, PSK auth, tunnel mode, matching local_ts/remote_ts).

Diagnosed two OPNsense-specific gaps: (1) swanctl connections require the legacy top-level <ipsec><enable> flag or ipsec_configure_do() aborts before writing swanctl.conf; (2) the enc0/IPsec pseudo-interface must be dynamically registered into config.xml's <interfaces> (via plugins_interfaces()+write_config) before a filter rule referencing interface 'enc0' compiles into a real pf rule; fixed both and reloaded.

Configured node3/node4 private-side addressing via nmcli static profiles (not raw `ip addr add`) after discovering NetworkManager was reconciling/wiping manually-assigned IPs on enp8s0 (RHEL10 reconciler anti-pattern).
Verified bidirectional ping node3<->node4 across the tunnel and confirmed via tcpdump on node1's transit interface that only ESP packets are visible on the wire (no plaintext ICMP).
Captured pre-restart boot markers (kern.boottime on OPNsense nodes, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on Linux nodes) and healthy-state evidence (swanctl SAs, pf rules, ping) for all 4 nodes.
Restarted node3, node4, node1, node2 one at a time (native reboot/`/sbin/reboot`), polling until exec access returned, and confirmed each node's boot marker changed.

After each restart, verified recovery: node3/node4 reapplied private addressing (persistent via nmcli after the fix) and re-verified ping; node1/node2 auto-recovered interfaces, IKE/child SAs, and the enc0 pf rule entirely from persisted config.xml with no manual intervention needed.

Flagged to the user (without acting on it) that local scratch files /tmp/node1_ipsec.py and /tmp/node2_ipsec.py were altered on disk by an unexplained external change mid-session; this did not affect the actual applied node configuration, which was verified independently via live swanctl/pf output.

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2 over the transit network
evidence.summary: swanctl --list-sas shows IKEv2 SA ESTABLISHED and child SA INSTALLED (TUNNEL, local 10.10.10.0/24, remote 10.20.20.0/24) on node1, mirrored on node2.

evidence.requirement: Private networks (lan-a/lan-b) carried over the tunnel; node3 and node4 reach each other by private address
evidence.summary: node3 pings node4's private IP 10.20.20.2 with 0% loss; node4 pings node3's private IP 10.10.10.2 with 0% loss; ESP byte/packet counters increment on node1's child SA confirming real traffic flow.

evidence.requirement: Traffic is encrypted in transit across the shared transit network
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's transit interface (vtnet1) during a node3->node4 ping shows only ESP(spi=...) packets between 10.99.99.1 and 10.99.99.2 in both directions — no plaintext ICMP visible on the wire.

evidence.requirement: Private networks have no other path between them (isolated except via the tunnel)
evidence.summary: node3 and node4 each only have their private-side NIC (enp8s0) reachable via node1/node2 respectively, with no direct L2 adjacency between lan-a and lan-b; the only path confirmed working is through the IPsec tunnel.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id e625b9a5... before restart; reboot acknowledged; connection timeout confirms disconnection; boot_id changed to 8db38fa6... after restart; reapplied static IP recovered tunnel ping to node4.

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id 7223d5b7... before restart; reboot acknowledged; connection errors confirm disconnection; boot_id changed to f10a7ae7... after restart; reapplied static IP recovered tunnel ping to node3.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: kern.boottime 17:03:06 before restart; reboot acknowledged; SSH timeout confirms disconnection; kern.boottime changed to 17:22:12 after restart; interfaces, IKE/child SA, and enc0 pf rule all recovered automatically from persisted config.xml with no manual reconfiguration.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: kern.boottime 17:03:06 before restart (unchanged baseline); reboot acknowledged; SSH timeout confirms disconnection; kern.boottime changed to 17:24:53 after restart; interfaces, IKE/child SA, and enc0 pf rule all recovered automatically from persisted config.xml.

evidence.requirement: Full end-to-end verification after all four node restarts complete
evidence.summary: Post-restart, node3->node4 ping (10.20.20.2) and node4->node3 ping (10.10.10.2) both succeed with 0% packet loss, confirming the tunnel and private-network reachability survived a full restart cycle of all managed nodes.
